full_judgment:
Mr. A.M. Mahmudur Rahman, J: In this Rule the question falls for determination is whether the impugned order dated 31.7.90 directing the petitioners to publish the result of B.A. (Hon's) examination of the opposite-party 1 held in 1978 should not be set aside. This case has got a chequered career. The opposite party 1 appeared in B.A. (Hon's) examination for the year 1976 held in 1978 from Comilla Victoria College. After publication of the result he found that he failed. He challenged the result in Title Suit No. 745 of 1979 in the Court of Munsif. 3rd Court, Comilla and sought for declaration that he passed the examination and the result declared by the University of Chittagong was illegal and not binding on him. The suit was resisted by the petitioners by filing written statement. The trial court by its judgment dated August. 30, 1983 decreed the suit holding that the result of B.A. (Hon's) Examination of 1976 of the opposite-party 1 held in the month of June. 1978 was illegal and the defendant-petitioners 1-2 including another were directed to arrange publication of the result of the plaintiff afresh on computation of the average mark of the marks obtained by the opposite party 1 in all papers except the tutorial papers adding the average mark as mark obtained in the tutorial papers to total mark obtained by him in all other papers. 

 2. Against that decree the petitioners appeal to the learned District Judge was dismissed for default followed by an application under Or. 41 R/19 C.P.C. for re-admission of the appeal accompanied by an application for condonation of delay in filing the appeal and Miscellaneous case No. 46 of 1984 was stated. The opposite party filed an application for rejection of the Miscellaneous Case on the ground of limitation. The appellate Court dismissed the Miscellaneous Case No. 46 of 1984 and the order of dismissal was followed by Miscellaneous Case No. 83 of 1986 for review of the said order unsuccessfully. Thereafter the petitioners filed Civil Revision No. 142 of 1987 in the High Court Division again unsuccessfully. Thereafter the opposite party 1 filed an application under Or. 89, R 2.(3) read with S. 151 C.P.C. for guilty of negligence and for contempt of court for showing dishonour to the order of the court in not publishing the result within 30 days as directed by the trial court. The petitioners resisted that application by filing written statement stating that the average mark computed was added to the total marks obtained by the opposite party 1 and the average marks worked out was 21 and that Was the mark given in tutorial and 16 marks in viva voce examination which the opposite-party 1 already got and he even so adding the mark was declared failed and this result was communicated to him by registered post on September 16, 1989 it was further stated that the delay was unintentional in publishing the result afresh and there was no laches and negligence on their part and no dishonor was shown to the order of the court and prayed for unconditional apology. The learned Assistant Judge, however, converted the said application suo mote into an application under Or. 21 R. 32 and started Execution Case No. 19 of 1989 and on contest passed the impugned order. 

 3. Mr. Omar Faruque appearing for the petitioners submits that the impugned order is misconceived in that it does not fall within the ambit of Or. 21 R 32 C.P.C. Or. 21 R .32 C.P.C. provides that where a party against whom a decree for Specific Performance of Contract or for restitution of conjugal rights or for an injunction has been passed and he wilfully failed to obey the order the decree may be enforced by restitution of conjugal life and in the case of Specific Performance of Contract or injunction by detention in civil prison or by attachment of his property or by both. Now the question is whether the order passed in the suit for publication of result as directed by the trial court partakes the nature of a mandatory injunction and if so whether the petitioners for wilful disobeying the same are liable for the detention in civil imprisonment or their properties are liable for attachment within the meaning of Or. 21 R. 32 C.P.C. Where on evidence it is proved that the petitioners wilfully disobeyed the order of the court in my opinion, they are liable for civil imprisonment or attachment of the property of the university on the strength of Sub-rule (2) of R. 32 of Or. 21 C.P.C. Thereafter, the contention of Mr. Omar Faruque does not appeal me though the order was passed in suit for declaration that the publication of result of an examination by the university is illegal and not binding upon the plaintiff. 

 4. Let us now proceed to examine whether in the facts and circumstances of the case this court sitting in revisional jurisdiction can exercise its power under Section 151 (1) C.P.C. for securing the end of justice. Although the trial court directed to arrive at an average mark on the basis of the marks obtained in 8 general papers it appears that in general papers the opposite party 1 obtained 322 and the average of the same came to 40.25. Out of this 40.25 he was given 21 mark for the tutorial papers (Full mark for tutorial is 50) but other half of 40.25 was not given to him for viva voce. Mr. Faruque argued that as the opposite party 1 already obtained 16 marks in viva voce he was not given other half of 40.25 in viva voce in place of 16 marks obtained by him. In support of the publication of the result afresh he submits that there was no violation of the order of the court in publishing the result afresh in as much as that was done in compliance with the order of the trial court. Mr. Faruque further argued that the opposite party No. 1 is entitled only 50% of 40.25 as that was the average of the 8 papers and the total marks in tutorial was 50. Therefore, 21 marked was added to the total marks as directed by the court but still then he got plucked. The plaintiff suit rests on the assertion that he got plucked as the marks obtained by him in the total tutorial classes were not sent to the University before publication of the result. Had it been sent he ought to have been declared passed. It is in evidence that at best opposite party 1 in one tutorial paper obtained 49% mark, Ext. 2 (B). From careful examination to Ext. 2 (B) I find that he obtained 49% in tutorial in one paper. I think that instead of the aver-age mark obtained in .8 general papers and adding half of the same to the total marks 322 obtained in general papers is not required on the very face of evidence. Ext. 2(B). inasmuch as a candidate who successfully passed in all the subjects should not suffer for the negligence of the authority of person who was at fault not to send the tutorial mark obtained by the opposite party 1 before publication of the result to the university. It is in consonance with the wisdom and justice that a boy who got 49% marks in one tutorial paper and when it is in the evidence that authorities did not send the tutorial marks to the university before publication of the result the conduct of the university authority to play in such a fashion with the fact of the student to the deprivation of his legal right should not be encouraged for no fault of the student. Therefore, I modify the order passed by the trial court. 49% mark obtained in one tutorial paper means 24.50 marks out of total 50 marks for tutorial papers. Therefore, I direct to add this 24.50 to the total marks i.e. 322 obtained by opposite party 1. 

 6. Accordingly, I discharge the Rule with the aforesaid modification of the impugned order. However, the modification based on calculation on the method adopted by me shall only govern this case and shall not be construed a general rule of calculation to be adopted in other cases.
